title: Peter Carlsson Hands Over Northvolt With One Week of Cash Left
dek: In November 2024 Northvolt filed for Chapter 11 with about a week of cash, and its co-founder stepped down, saying the timing had been over-ambitious.

story.event: Stepping down as chief executive the day after Northvolt filed for Chapter 11, ahead of its bankruptcy in Sweden
story.summary: On 21 November 2024 Northvolt, the Swedish battery maker co-founded by Peter Carlsson and Paolo Cerruti, filed for Chapter 11 in the United States with about $30 million in cash and $5.8 billion in debts; the next day Carlsson stepped down as chief executive, saying the company had been over-ambitious on timing. New financing never arrived, and on 12 March 2025 Northvolt AB and four Swedish subsidiaries filed for bankruptcy in Sweden, with about 5,000 people still employed. Lyten completed its purchase of the Swedish plants in February 2026.
paragraphs: On Friday 22 November 2024, Peter Carlsson told reporters he was stepping down as chief executive of Northvolt, the Swedish battery maker he had co-founded in 2016 and run ever since. The day before, it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States, with about $30 million in cash, enough for roughly a week, and debts of $5.8 billion. "Personally this is an emotional day," he said. The company had been "like a baby" to him.

Northvolt was meant to anchor Europe's effort to make its own electric-car batteries instead of relying on Chinese suppliers. Carlsson, a former Tesla executive, and his co-founder Paolo Cerruti had drawn more than $10 billion in equity, debt and public financing and built a gigafactory, Northvolt Ett, at Skellefteå in northern Sweden. Steady output took far longer than planned. In 2024 BMW dropped a €2 billion order over production delays, and in September Northvolt announced 1,600 job cuts. By November, one production line was delivering finished cells to a customer, the truckmaker Scania.

Chapter 11 let the company keep operating while it restructured. It brought about $245 million, $100 million of it from Scania, but Carlsson said $1 billion to $1.2 billion was needed. Advisers sought partners, with a liquidation firm on standby. "In hindsight, we were over-ambitious on the timing in which we could achieve it," he said. He called it a good moment to hand over "to the next generation of leaders", and stayed on the board as a senior adviser.

Output did improve. By March 2025 the company said its serial lines were making twice as many cells as in September, with yields up by half. The money did not follow. On 12 March, with a tax payment of 291 million kronor falling due, Northvolt AB and four Swedish subsidiaries filed for bankruptcy in Sweden. About 5,000 people still worked for the group; Sweden's wage guarantee covered unpaid pay only up to 235,200 kronor a person. "This is an incredibly difficult day for everyone at Northvolt," said the interim chairman, Tom Johnstone. Cerruti had stepped aside as head of the North American business in January. In February 2026 the American firm Lyten completed its purchase of the Swedish plants and announced plans to rehire.

quote.text: simple and manageable undertakings proceed according to the pleasure of the person in charge of them, but enormous ones, beyond his capacity to manage, are not easily undertaken. When he has got them to administer, they hinder him, and press hard upon him, and just as he thinks that success is within his grasp, they collapse
quote.work: Of Anger (De Ira), in the Minor Dialogues
quote.locator: Book III, chapter VII (the fifth book of the Dialogues, addressed to Novatus)
quote.source_title: Minor Dialogues, Together With the Dialogue on Clemency, tr. Aubrey Stewart, Project Gutenberg eBook #64576
quote.connection: Seneca warns that enormous undertakings slip from the hands of those running them just as success seems near, and Northvolt's yields were rising when the money ran out. Yet its whole premise was that a small European battery maker could not compete, so his counsel of manageable work may never have been on offer.

reflection: Carlsson's own verdict was not that the goal was wrong but that the timing was. That distinction is worth keeping. A plan can be right in its direction and still wrong about how soon, and the gap between the two is usually paid for by other people: staff, suppliers, a town that had built itself around a factory.

You will make promises about dates, to colleagues, to a first customer, to your family and to yourself. They hold better when the slow parts are counted in, the training, the faults nobody has met yet, the weeks when you are tired, rather than the pace of your best month.
invitation: Take one deadline you have given someone this month and write down what it assumes will go smoothly. If the list is long, move the date today, while moving it is still cheap.

cross_checks.claim: Northvolt filed for Chapter 11 on 21 November 2024 and Carlsson stepped down as chief executive the next day, staying on the board as senior adviser.
At filing Northvolt had about $30 million in cash and about $5.8 billion in debts.
Chapter 11 gave access to about $245 million, including $100 million from Scania.
BMW dropped a €2 billion order over production delays, and in September 2024 Northvolt announced 1,600 job cuts.
On 12 March 2025 Northvolt AB and four Swedish subsidiaries filed for bankruptcy in Sweden, with about 5,000 people employed.
Lyten completed its purchase of Northvolt's Swedish plants in early 2026 and planned to restart and rehire.

research_notes: Headcount: Reuters (22 November 2024) gave about 6,600 staff in seven countries before the Chapter 11 restructuring; in March 2025 Northvolt's release said over 5,000 employees, interim chairman Tom Johnstone (The Local) said close to 5,000 still employed, and AFP/Fortune said about 5,000. The story uses 'about 5,000' for March 2025 and does not use the November figure. September 2024 cuts: 1,600 announced (The Local, Fortune); The Local adds that after negotiations slightly more than 1,300 were laid off; the story says 1,600 were announced. Money raised: Reuters gives more than $10 billion in equity, debt and public financing since 2016; The Local gives owners' capital of about 90 billion kronor and debt of about 60 billion kronor, a different measure; the story uses Reuters's phrasing. Debts: $5.8 billion (Reuters; Fortune citing the Chapter 11 filings) and $5.84 billion (The Local citing Swedish media); the story says $5.8 billion. Chapter 11 money: CNBC's $245 million is the sum of the $145 million cash collateral and $100 million from Scania that The Local reports separately. Founding year: Reuters, CNBC, pv magazine and Fortune say 2016; The Local says 2015 (electrive, which blocks the checker, notes the company began as SGF Energy); the story uses 2016. BMW: The Local dates the cancelled order to May 2024; the story says only 'in 2024'. Funding is set to 'mixed' rather than the slate's 'venture' because Reuters describes the money as equity, debt and public financing (the EIB, Swedish pension funds and corporate shareholders such as Volkswagen alongside Goldman Sachs). Blame: the story gives only Carlsson's own words ('over-ambitious on the timing') and the company's stated reasons; Reuters's unnamed company sources on machine faults and inexperienced staff, and press questions about Carlsson's earlier share sales, are not used. Paolo Cerruti is described by Northvolt as a co-founder; the story notes he stepped aside as North America CEO on 30 January 2025 and remained chairman of that entity. Lyten's own completion release (lyten.com, URL dated 26 February, text dated 27 February 2026) blocks the checker, so completion is sourced to Just Auto and Industry Insider. The Seneca passage is from Of Anger, Book III, chapter VII, in Stewart's numbering of the Dialogues (the fifth book); it is about managing one's affairs to keep the mind at peace and is applied here by analogy.
